newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on bullish USDA crop report.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on bullish USDA crop report.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher, although new crop contracts outpaced nearbys on bullishness over the USDA crop report.
New crop months were bolstered by Friday's USDA winter wheat seedings estimate, which pegged winter wheat acreage at a 19-year low, traders said.

"It was not a bullish report for the old crop but it was for the new," a trader said. The (supply/demand data) portrayed some minor increases in carryouts for hard and soft wheat. Overall, all-wheat supply and demand increased, so that put some pressure on the front end."
Winter wheat seedings for the 1997 crop were estimated at 48.22 million acres, well below the average projection in the Reuter analysts survey of 51.40 million.
Hard red winter wheat seedings were estimated at 34.1 million acres, down five percent from last year.

KCBT wheat closed 1/4 to 10-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 1/4 cent at $4.11-1/2. March had been as high as $4.22. July settled up 10-1/4 cents at $3.62, its highest close since Dec. 18. The July contract also posted its largest daily gain since Aug. 12, when the contract gained 13 cents.

Traders said the featured player was Prudential, which sold 1.5 million March, one million May and one million July bushels. Prudential also bought one million March. Refco sold two million March and Shay Grain sold one million March.
